questions.question: In which of the following market forms a firm does not exercise control over price?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is *__**Perfect Competition**__*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Perfect Competition:** In a market form characterized by perfect competition, firms do not have control over the price of the products they sell. Prices are determined by the forces of supply and demand in the market. Since there are many sellers offering identical products, no single firm can influence the market price.
 
• **Price Takers:** Firms in a perfect competition market are known as "price takers," meaning they must accept the prevailing market price and cannot set prices above or below it. Any attempt to change the price would result in losing customers to competitors.
 
• *Hence, option 4 (Perfect Competition) is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Perfect Competition:** Perfect competition is characterized by a large number of buyers and sellers, homogenous products, free entry and exit of firms, and perfect information. These factors contribute to the inability of individual firms to influence prices.
 
• **Market Equilibrium:** In perfect competition, the market reaches equilibrium where the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded at the prevailing price, ensuring that the market clears without any excess supply or demand.
 
• **Economic Efficiency:** Perfect competition leads to economic efficiency, as firms produce at the lowest possible cost, and consumers pay the lowest possible price, resulting in optimal allocation of resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparison with Other Market Forms:** In contrast to perfect competition, market forms like monopoly and oligopoly allow firms to exert some control over prices due to the lack of competition or the presence of few sellers.
 
• **Real-World Examples:** While perfect competition is a theoretical construct, some agricultural markets, where many farmers sell identical products like wheat or corn, come close to this model.
 
• **Consumer Benefit:** Consumers benefit from perfect competition as it typically results in lower prices and a higher level of product availability.

questions.question: Which of the following is represented by 'Lorenz Curve'?
questions.solution: Lorenz curve is a graphical representation of the distribution of income or of wealth. It was developed by Max O. Lorenz in 1905 for representing inequality of the wealth distribution. It is often used in income distribution and business modeling.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a fundamental duty?

options.text: To abide by the Constitution and respect the National Flag
To uphold and protect the sovereignty
Abolition of titles except military and academic

questions.solution:
• Fundamental Duties are the moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• They were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• There are, in total, 11 fundamental duties in the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Which article can be used by the President of India to declare financial emergency?
questions.solution:
Using Article 360, the President of India can impose financial emergency, when a situation arises whereby the financial stability or the credit of India or any part thereof is threatened. No emergency under Article 360 has been issued so far.

**Trick: Emergency articles starts from (352 and then add + 4 + 4 that is 352, 356, 360)**

questions.question: The Poona Pact was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and __________.
questions.solution: The Poona Pact agreement was signed between B. R. Ambedkar and M. K. Gandhi on the reservation of electoral seats for the depressed classes in the legislature of then British India. It was signed on 24th of September 1932 at Yerwada Central Jail in Poona.

questions.question: Which Governor General abolished the 'Sati System' in India?
questions.solution: Lord Wiliam Bentinck played a vital role in abolishing Sati System in India. He declared the practice of Sati illegal by the regulation number XVII of December 1829. In this regulation he declared that the practice of Sati in any form was illegal and the practitioners would be liable to be incriminated by the courts.

questions.concept: Science Technology and Inventions, Ecology and Environment
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a primary green house gas in the earth's atmosphere?
questions.solution: Hydrogen is not a primary green house gas as it does not absorb and emit radiant energy within the thermal infrared range. The primary greenhouse gases in Earth's atmosphere are water vapor, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, and ozone.

questions.question: Which type of forest is most widespread in India?
questions.solution:
• **Tropical Deciduous Forests **are the most widespread forests in India.
 
• They are generally found in in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Orissa and parts of Maharastra.
 
• They are generally found in tropical areas with a dry season that still has enough moisture for tree growth.

questions.question: Which blood group is universal donor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2, i.e. **__O-__**

__
 
• **O- blood type is the universal red blood cell donor because their red blood cells can be transfused into any patient, regardless of blood type.** 
 
• Those with O- can only receive from other O- donors.
 
• O- red cells must be used for trauma situations and other emergencies when the patient’s blood type is not known.
 
• O- red cells are also frequently used for babies and sickle cell anemia patients.
 
• O- makes up only 6.6% of the population, found in just 1 of every 15 people.
 
• **O+ can give red blood cells to any positive blood types.**
 
• Those with O+ can only receive red cells from O+ or O- donors.
 
• O+ is found in 38% of people, making it the most common blood type.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Blood groups are determined by **ABO blood grouping** and **Rh factors**.
 
• The ABO system is based on the antigens A and B that are produced on the RBCs.
 
• The Rh factor confers the positive or negative Rh factor associated with the ABO blood groups.
 
• When we refer to the ABO blood grouping only, we usually just say that blood group O is the universal donor.
 
• However, if we consider the Rh factor along with ABO blood grouping, then **O negative blood group is the actual universal blood donor**.
 
• This is because it has **no antigens (A or B)** and also **lack Rh factor**.
 
• Rh negative blood groups do not have Rh factor and hence, can be accepted by even people with Rh positive blood groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

 
• 
 
Though O+ blood can be donated to people with A, B, AB and O blood groups, but it is not called universal blood group. Because it is still risky for people with Rh negative blood.

questions.question: In how many parts is the human brain divided?
questions.solution:
The brain has three major parts or regions, namely the __fore-brain, mid-brain, and hind-brain.__

__The fore-brain:__

__
 
• It is the main thinking part of the brain.
 
• It is considered to be the most important part of the brain because it performs all cognitive, emotional, and motor activities.
 
• Separate areas of the fore-brain are specialized for hearing, smell, sight, and so on.

The mid-brain:__

__
 
• The midbrain is relatively small in size and it connects the hindbrain with the forebrain.
 
• A few neural centers related to some special reflexes and visual and auditory sensations are found here.
 
• An important part of the midbrain, known as the Reticular Activating System (RAS), is responsible for our arousal. It makes us alert and active by regulating sensory inputs.

The Hind Brain:__

 
• Its main components are medulla oblongata, cerebellum, and pons.
 
• This part of the brain regulates basic life-supporting activities like breathing, heart rate, and blood pressure.
 
• It also maintains and controls posture and equilibrium of the body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dce508cceb20bc1dbb1468fcdb2031fd5aaf9099a966da4ae29137a1ace43102.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b9b3ceb4ec2845223ade9281a6837d6e3bcc038d4a7206f9ad2c6fbd095607a.png]

questions.question: In which of the following class can we put Adrenaline?
questions.solution: Adrenaline is a hormone that plays an important role in the fight-or-flight response by increasing blood flow to muscles, output of the heart, pupil dilation, and blood sugar. The adrenaline hormone is produced by both the adrenal glands and certain neurons.

questions.question: Supercooling is cooling of liquid ________.
questions.solution: Supercooling is the process of lowering the temperature of a liquid or a gas below its freezing point without it becoming a solid. The process of supercooling requires that water be pure and free of nucleation sites.

questions.question: When light passes from one medium to another there is a change in its direction, this phenomenon is called ________.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Total Internal reflection: The total reflection of light from a higher refractive index medium to back in its medium at an angle more than a critical angle known as total internal reflection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/951e7d6c53c2e1c59b05637d34a6559653ee83c4100cda16d262d571579473c2.png] 

 
• Refraction: When a ray of light passes from one medium to another it suffers a change in direction at the boundary of two media is called refraction.

 
 
• The change in direction because the speed of light travels at different speeds in different mediums. Refractive Index of a medium defines that it is denser or rarer
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82339a0de627554b07235929cdd32b43851718b65b7114397e275f2df207692c.png] 

**Explanation:**__

 
• As we all know, Light is electromagnetic radiation, which always **propagates **in a straight line.

 
 
• And refraction is the change in direction of a wave, caused by the change in the wave's speed.
 
• As a result, it **bends toward or away from normal** (change its direction) when it p**ropagates from one medium to another** as we can see above.
 
 
 
• Whereas in total normal reflection there is no change of medium throughout its propagation.
 
• Hence option **1 is correct** among all

questions.question: Which among the following is not an input device?
questions.solution: A plotter is a computer printer for printing vector graphics and is used in applications such as computer-aided design. Plotters are used to print designs of ships and machines, plans for buildings. Plotter is not an input device as it gives a hard copy of the output.

questions.question: Which of the following is also known as Carbolic Acid?
questions.solution: Phenol is also known as Carbolic Acid. It is a white, crystalline, water-soluble, poisonous mass obtained from coal tar or a hydroxyl derivative of benzene. It is primarily used to synthesize plastics and related materials.

questions.question: Who discovered electron?
questions.solution: The electron was discovered by J.J Thomon. Thomson's experiments with cathode ray tubes showed that all atoms contain tiny negatively charged subatomic particles or electrons.

questions.question: Who is a major driving force behind the 'Narmada Bachao Andolan'?
questions.solution: Narmada Bachao Andolan is a social movement against the number of large dams being built across the Narmada River, which flows through the states of Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. The major driving force behind the “Narmada Bachao Andolan” is Medha Patkar.

questions.question: 'Udey Desh ka Aam Nagrik' (UDAN) scheme for regional air connectivity will provide travel to tier 2 and tier 3 cities at the rate of Rs ________ per hour.
questions.solution: Under the UDAN Scheme people travelling to tier 2 and tier 3 cities will have to pay Rs 2500 per hour. The objective of UDAN is aimed at making air travel affordable and widespread, to boost inclusive national economic development and air transport infrastructure development of all regions and states of India.

questions.question: Who invented radar?
questions.solution:
• Heinrich Hertz invented the radar.
 
• Radar is an object-detection system that uses radio waves to determine the range, angle, or velocity of objects.
 
• It can be used to detect aircraft, ships, spacecraft, guided missiles etc.

questions.question: David Warner plays cricket for which country?
questions.solution: David Warner is an Australian cricketer and the current vice-captain of the Australian cricket team. He is a destructive, fiery left-handed opening batsman who became the first Australian cricketer in 132 years to get into the national team without playing a first-class game.

questions.question: Japanese art ‘Ikebana’ is related to ________.
questions.solution: Ikebana is the Japanese art of flower arrangement. It is one of the traditional arts of Japan, has been practiced for more than 600 years. It developed from the Buddhist ritual of offering flowers to the spirits of the dead.

questions.question: Who was awarded the 2017 Padma Bhushan Award in the field of Art-Music?
questions.solution: The 2017 Padma Bhushan Award in the field of Art-Music was awarded to Vishwa Mohan Bhatt. Bhatt is a Grammy-winning Hindustani classical music instrumentalist who plays the Mohan Veena. He is best known for his Grammy award winning album “A Meeting by the River with Ry Cooder”.

questions.question: Who has recently launched his autobiography titled 'An Unsuitable Boy'?
questions.solution: Karan Johar launched his autobiography “An Unsuitable Boy” that narrates different events of his life starting from his childhood.

questions.question: Which of the following country is not a member of 'The Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA)'?
questions.solution: Indian Ocean Rim Association is an international organisation consisting of coastal states bordering the Indian Ocean. The Association comprises 21 member states and 7 dialogue partners. China is not a member of IORA but is the dialogue partner of IORA.

questions.question: Which country has launched the longest bullet train line covering a distance of 2252 kilometers in January, 2017?
questions.solution: China launched the longest bullet train line in January 2017. The Kunming-Guiyang railway, is part of the Shanghai-Kunming line, and at 2,252 kilometers it is the longest of China's east-west rail lines.
